topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: It opens the lecture by framing the importance and complexity of the complement system.

topics.label: Core principles and nomenclature of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: They establish the overarching structure, naming conventions, and central role of C3 cleavage in complement function.

topics.label: Mechanisms of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the three upstream pathways that recognize pathogens and converge to activate C3.

topics.label: Downstream effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the primary effector outcomes of complement activation, including opsonization, inflammation, and pathogen lysis.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and host cell protection
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the regulatory mechanisms and proteins that protect host tissues from unintended complement destruction.

topics.label: Clinical manifestations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It details the pathological consequences and disease patterns resulting from deficiencies in different complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the evolutionary strategies and mechanisms used by pathogens, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, to evade complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the closing remarks for the lecture and previews the upcoming topic.
